ladder.name: Rope and Head Load
ladder.idea: Workers loop goods with a rope and carry them out on their heads. Slow, cheap, and the player can always do it too.

ladder.name: Wheelbarrow and Hand Cart
ladder.idea: Wheels but no engine: barrows, push carts, trolleys and pallet jacks. No fuel, bigger loads, a little slower on rough ground.

ladder.name: Cargo Tricycle
ladder.idea: A three-wheeler with a load bed zips between rows or stacks. First engine, first fuel bill, first horn.

ladder.name: Pickup and Small Truck
ladder.idea: A four-wheel pickup, van or motor boat takes a whole row or stack per trip and parks at the station door.

ladder.name: Tractor, Forklift, Winch
ladder.idea: Heavy machines lift instead of people: tractor and trailer in fields, forklift in yards, net winch on water.

ladder.name: Full Sweep Fleet
ladder.idea: A harvester or reach truck clears the whole field or yard in one pass and feeds a big truck. The manager can dispatch it.

rules: Every machine needs a hired driver or operator and fuel in the tank. No driver or empty tank means it parks and the rope crew takes over.
The rope never goes away. The player and farmhands can always hand-carry, and hand carrying costs no fuel, so it is the fallback.
Machines never make the player idle. The player rides along, picks the route, refuels, and taps to unload for a bonus.
Each tier is bought on a price pad at the field or yard gate. The old tool stays as a spare for the next line or a new branch.
A machine carries only as much as stations and storage can take. If the store is full it waits, so upgrade stations with it.
Tiers 5 and 6 need a trained operator. Training costs money and a short wait. Untrained staff cannot start heavy machines.
Same six tiers for all ten businesses. Only the model changes: field, pasture, water or yard. One system to learn.

fuelAndMaintenance.howItWorks: Fuel costs 1,400 naira a litre. Tricycle burns 1 litre per 10 trips, pickup 1 per 4, tractor or forklift 1 per 2, top fleet 2 per trip. Service every 200 trips costs 2% of the purchase price. Skip it and speed drops 30% until a mechanic fixes it. Tiers 1 and 2 burn nothing.
fuelAndMaintenance.realBasis: Petrol sold at about 1,410 to 1,450 naira a litre in September 2026 and diesel averaged about 1,410. Tricycle riders report fuel as their biggest yearly cost, and servicing is by hours used.

research.claim: A new passenger tricycle cost at least 3.5 million naira outright in January 2025, up from about 600,000 naira five years earlier.
A 2026 price list puts 50hp to 75hp tractors at 12.5 to 22 million naira and 12hp to 18hp walking tractors at 2.5 to 4 million naira.
Refurbished imported tractors of popular older models are listed at 15 to 28 million naira in 2026.
Used diesel forklifts offered to Nigerian buyers range from about 2,000 to 63,000 euros, with a 2024 three-tonne unit near 7,200 euros or about 10.8 million naira.
A used medium refrigerated truck is listed for Nigerian buyers at 19,950 euros, roughly 30 million naira before shipping and duty.
Filling stations in Abuja sold petrol at 1,410 to 1,450 naira a litre in September 2026 and tricycle fares rose 100 to 200 naira.
The national statistics office put the average diesel price at 1,409.61 naira a litre in November 2025.
A survey reported tricycle operators in three states spend about 2.5 million naira a year on fuel.
